facts.text: The module defines the topic names rt/lowcmd, rt/arm_sdk and rt/lowstate
The controller publishes LowCmd on rt/arm_sdk when motion_mode is true and on rt/lowcmd otherwise
The controller subscribes to LowState on rt/lowstate
The constructor joins DDS domain 1 in simulation mode and domain 0 on the real robot
After initializing the DDS endpoints and starting the subscriber thread, the constructor blocks until the first LowState message arrives; the loop has no timeout
The control period is control_dt = 1/250 s
The clip is current_q + delta / max(motion_scale, 1.0) with motion_scale = max(abs(delta)) / (velocity_limit * control_dt)
The constructor starts the publisher thread as a daemon
The publisher loops indefinitely, reads the stored arm targets and writes LowCmd at the control period; it does not check for a stop acknowledgement
The constructor enables motor modes and position gains for all G1 joints, including the non-arm joints
ctrl_dual_arm stores q_target and tauff_target under ctrl_lock and returns nothing; it sends no command of its own
G1_29_JointArmIndex lists the left arm joints 15 to 21 and the right arm joints 22 to 28, in that order
get_current_dual_arm_q returns the fourteen arm joint positions and get_current_dual_arm_dq their velocities from the subscribed LowState buffer
ctrl_dual_arm_go_home sets q_target to zeros and waits up to 100 attempts of 0.05 s for the joints to come within 0.05 rad of zero; it is a move to the home pose, not a stop
The class defines no stop, disable, brake or emergency method
The controller's arm_velocity_limit starts at 20.0; this is a controller setting, not the joint travel range
speed_instant_max sets arm_velocity_limit to 30.0
The publisher's gradual-speed branch uses a hard-coded 5 s ramp from 20.0 to 30.0
The package imports unitree_sdk2py for the DDS channel, the IDL messages and the CRC
pyproject.toml leaves the unitree_sdk2py dependency commented out, so the clone does not install the DDS transport
EvalRealConfig defaults arm to G1_29
setup_robot_interface constructs the selected arm controller with motion_mode and simulation_mode
The README describes eval_robot as the real-machine inference verification of the model

safe_state.description: no safe state is confirmed: the e-stop requests the last buffered arm positions with zero feedforward torque, then fails SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED with the latch held; the undated buffer may be stale, the daemon continues publishing and may still have a previous target in flight, and non-arm motor commands remain enabled
